title: Model-tailored outlier normalization and layer stability patch for FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: During recent FP8/INT8 calibration sweeps we observed model-specific failure modes where global per-tensor rescale strategies cause distributional collapse in some layers and spuriously large logits in others. This is most pronounced for Qwen and certain Mistral families on long-context evals and for Llama variants with adapter layers. Problem: Our current calibration pipeline applies a single global clipping and scale finder per weight-tensor, which underestimates rare but high-magnitude activation spikes (outliers). Those outliers then produce large relative quantization error after folding and lead to downstream accuracy regressions (generation instability, token repetition, degraded BLEU/perplexity). Proposal: Implement a model-tailored outlier normalization step and a lightweight per-layer stability patch that are applied as part of the calibration harness. Key ideas: 1) Per-layer percentile-based clipping with adjustable tail weight (e.g., 99.9/99.99 percentiles) and an additional head-wise gating multiplier for multi-head attention layers. 2) Adaptive rescale annealing: compute an initial robust scale using trimmed variance, then anneal per-batch to a final scale to avoid large one-off adjustments driven by noisy calibration batches. 3) Small per-channel clamp limits for output-projection layers to protect softmax inputs. 4) Integration points: this runs after calibration trace collection and before quant-parameter export. It exposes knobs for FP8/INT8 paths separately (different clipping targets). Rationale: Percentile clipping preserves the bulk distribution while explicitly dealing with the long tail. Annealing reduces sensitivity to sample ordering. Head-wise multiplers let us target attention-head spikes without globally penalizing other parameters. Validation: add a regression suite (generation stability, classification accuracy, perplexity) per model-family and a gate to compare baseline vs patched profile. Performance tradeoffs: small additional CPU cost in calibration for trace aggregation, negligible inference CPU; expected quant size unchanged; expected small improvement in per-token latency due to fewer corrective fallbacks. Rollout: start as an opt-in profile in runtime-1.23, run canary on internal Dedicated pools and synthetic workloads, then flip default when we observe no regressions after 2 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces quant profiles with per-layer percentile clipping and annealed rescale parameters for Llama/Mistral/Qwen families
No >1% relative regression on our generation stability metric across the three model families on canary datasets
Unit tests for percentiles, annealing schedule, and head-wise gating added and passing in CI
Documentation (CONFLUENCE) describing knobs and recommended defaults for FP8 and INT8
steps: Add per-layer percentile statistics collector to calibration traces (99.0, 99.9, 99.99)
Implement annealed rescale algorithm with configurable schedule and minimum floor
Add head-wise multiplier support for attention layers and small per-channel clamps for output projections
Wire new profile export into existing quant-profile JSON with clear FP8 vs INT8 fields
Run validation suite across Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-7B on our regression harness
Open PR for runtime changes and follow with canary deployment to Dedicated test pool
Collect telemetry for 2 weeks, evaluate, and decide on default flip
progress_updates: 2026-02-18 - Ticket created by Aisha Patel: initial investigation notes and measured regressions for Qwen long-context perplexity.
2026-02-24 - Marco Li: added percentile collector prototype to calibration harness; initial runs show that 99.99 percentile identifies rare spikes not captured by mean/std approach.

2026-03-01 - Marco Li: implemented annealing schedule (linear 0.6->1.0 over 8 minibatches) and head-wise multiplier. Benchmarks: generation stability reduced token repetition by ~12% on Mistral-7B synthetic prompt set.
2026-03-04 - Internal review with Research (Sofia Aguilar): suggested lowering FP8 clip target slightly to avoid small degradation on math benchmarks; added A/B test plan.
2026-03-08 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3268 (calibration: percentile-clips + anneal). Automated tests passing locally; flagged for CI flakiness on cross-compile matrix.

2026-03-10 - Canary deploy to Dedicated test pool (canary-quant-52341): telemetry shows no increase in error rate; slight 2% median latency improvement under burst traffic due to fewer fallback model requests.

2026-03-12 - QA: ran extended validation for 48 hours against diverse prompt corpus. Observed minor BLEU drop (0.4) on a single Llama-variant; investigating whether clamp floor needs small adjustment.
notes: Trade-offs: tighter clipping reduces extreme quant error but can truncate legitimate signal; annealing mitigates abrupt truncation across calibration batches.
FP8 vs INT8: FP8 tends to tolerate slightly higher tail mass; we will use more aggressive clipping for INT8 by default.

Fallback policy: if a model-family shows >1% regression on its family-specific gate, the calibration job will attach a 'legacy' profile alongside the new profile and runtime will route based on rollout policy.
Future: consider per-head learned clamps discovered via small calibration-opt phase (ML-based) if hand-tuned percentiles are insufficient.
final_decision: Pending: adjust clamp floor for the affected Llama variant after targeted calibration run (expected decision by 2026-03-18).
